steps.body: The opposite case: when the variable cancels and leaves a TRUE statement like 3 = 3, EVERY value of x works — there are INFINITELY MANY solutions. Both sides are secretly the same expression.

panels.title: Step 1
panels.body: Subtract 2x from both sides. The x-terms cancel.

panels.title: Step 2
panels.body: You're left with 3 = 3 — always true, no x needed.

panels.title: Step 3
panels.body: Since 3 = 3 is ALWAYS true, every value of x works — infinitely many solutions.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — when the variable cancels and leaves a true statement, every x is a solution.

steps.body: This happens when both sides are the SAME after simplifying — same x-coefficient AND same constant. It's like two lines drawn exactly on top of each other: they share every point.

explanationVariants: 5x − 2 = 5x − 2: subtract 5x to get −2 = −2, always true — infinitely many.
Same x-coefficient AND same constant → true leftover statement → infinitely many.

choices.label: Infinitely many
choices.feedback: Right — both sides are identical, so every x works.

choices.label: No solution
choices.feedback: That needs a FALSE leftover statement — here −2 = −2 is TRUE, so infinitely many, not none.

choices.label: One solution
choices.feedback: The x-terms cancel and leave −2 = −2 (always true), so every x works — infinitely many, not one.

choices.label: x = 0
choices.feedback: Every x works, not just 0 — the equation is true for all values: infinitely many.

choices.label: 6 = 6, always true
choices.feedback: Right — distribute to 2x + 6 = 2x + 6; the x cancels, leaving 6 = 6: infinitely many solutions.

choices.label: 6 = 5, false
choices.feedback: Distributing 2(x+3) gives 2x + 6, matching the right side exactly — you get 6 = 6, true, not 6 = 5.

choices.label: x = 6, one solution
choices.feedback: The x-terms are identical (both 2x) and cancel — no single x-value; you get 6 = 6, always true.

choices.label: 2 = 2, one solution
choices.feedback: The leftover is 6 = 6, and it means infinitely many solutions, not one.

explanationVariants: 4(x + 1) = 4x + 4 expands to 4x + 4 = 4x + 4 — identical sides, so infinitely many.
Distributing gives the exact same expression on both sides → infinitely many.

widget.prompt: Which equation has INFINITELY many solutions?

options.label: 4(x + 1) = 4x + 4
options.feedback: Right — distribute to 4x + 4 = 4x + 4, identical sides: every x works.

options.label: 4(x + 1) = 4x + 5
options.feedback: Distributing gives 4x + 4 = 4x + 5, then 4 = 5 (false): no solution, not infinitely many.

options.label: 4(x + 1) = 5x + 4
options.feedback: Distributing gives 4x + 4 = 5x + 4 — different x-coefficients, so one solution.

options.label: 4x + 1 = 4x + 4
options.feedback: Same 4x but different constants (1 vs 4) → false leftover → no solution, not infinitely many.

explanationVariants: A true leftover (0 = 0) means infinitely many; a false leftover (0 = 5) means none. The difference is whether the constants match.
Cancelled variable + true statement = infinite; + false statement = none.

widget.prompt: After the variable cancels, you're left with 0 = 0. What does this mean?

options.label: Infinitely many solutions — it's always true
options.feedback: Right — 0 = 0 holds for every x, so all values are solutions.

options.label: No solution — the variable disappeared
options.feedback: The variable disappearing alone doesn't mean no solution — 0 = 0 is TRUE, so it's infinitely many.

options.label: One solution, x = 0
options.feedback: 0 = 0 has no x in it — it's true for EVERY x, giving infinitely many solutions.

options.label: The equation is broken
options.feedback: It's a valid outcome — 0 = 0 being always true means infinitely many solutions.

explanationVariants: For infinitely many, both sides must be identical: 5x + 3 = 5x + ▢ needs ▢ = 3 so the constants match too.
Match BOTH the x-coefficient and the constant → infinitely many.

widget.prompt: Which value of ▢ makes 5x + 3 = 5x + ▢ have INFINITELY many solutions?

options.feedback: Right — ▢ = 3 makes both sides identical (5x + 3 = 5x + 3), true for every x.

options.label: Any number except 3
options.feedback: That's the NO-solution case — a different constant makes the leftover false. To get infinitely many, ▢ must equal 3.
▢ = 0 gives 5x + 3 = 5x + 0, then 3 = 0 (false): no solution, not infinitely many.
▢ = 5 gives 3 = 5 (false) after cancelling: no solution. For infinitely many, ▢ must be 3.

hints: Infinitely many needs BOTH sides to be exactly the same expression.
The x-terms already match (5x = 5x). So the constant ▢ must EQUAL 3.
▢ = 3 makes both sides 5x + 3, true for every x — infinitely many solutions.

steps.body: Infinitely many solutions: the variable cancels and leaves a true statement.
takeaways: If x vanishes and you get a true statement (like 3 = 3), every x is a solution.
This happens when both sides simplify to the same expression.
Geometrically, it's one line drawn on top of itself.
